deck: Spoke: show this week's open slots (invented example)

brief.asks: What should Spoke build next quarter?
How will we know it worked?

slides.title: The goal is first bookings that complete, not downloads
slides.body: Shops pay when a repair gets booked. Downloads can grow while bookings do not.

slides.title: We build for the commuter who loses a workday to a broken bike
slides.body: We assume commuters are 60% of repair demand, and they are the only group that needs the bike back the same day.
footer_sources: Assumption, stated on the workshop board (frame 2)

slides.title: Today she calls three shops to find one that has a slot
slides.body: No shop shows its week. The price is unknown until the bike is on the stand.

slides.title: Four ideas, from a shared calendar to office pickup
slides.body: Open-slot calendar, fixed-price menu, loaner bike, office pickup. Each one answers one failure.

slides.title: The open-slot calendar removes the first reason a booking never starts
slides.body: Cheapest test: three shops update a shared sheet every morning. Its weak spot: it depends on shops keeping it current.

slides.title: Started bookings that complete should go from 40% to 55% in six weeks
slides.body: Guardrail: shop no-shows and cancellations do not rise.
footer_sources: Assumptions, stated on the workshop board (frame 6)

slides.title: Three shops by hand, then one neighborhood, then the city
slides.body: Each phase starts only if the completion rate held in the one before.

slides.title: One calendar, one number to watch, three shops to start

closing_sentence: For commuters who lose a workday to a broken bike, show this week's open slots and count how many started bookings complete
